thread:
lina.k: quick FYI, HF->Redwood conversion for mosaic-7b-quant hit a failing eval. failing examples show truncated context and kv-cache mismatch.

carlos: ugh, guess the config.json didn't map cleanly. which keys look off?

sasha: my bet is rope_scaling + max_position_embeddings combo. also saw num_key_value_heads mismatch in some HF forks.

lina.k: here's the model config snippet from HF tarball: 

```json
{
  "max_position_embeddings": 2048,
  "rope_scaling": { "factor": 1.1, "type": "linear" },
  "num_key_value_heads": 16,
  "sliding_window": 256
}
```

matt: RW runtime expects num_key_value_heads to either divide heads_per_layer or be absent (we remap internally). if it's present and mismatched we end up with reinterpreted head dims -> outputs degrade.

carlos: convert-bot output when running rw-convert: 

```
convert-bot: converted model mosaic-7b-quant, patched config.json: removed "num_key_value_heads" and set "max_position_embeddings": 1024 to match runtime.
WARN: rope_scaling type "linear" -> RW supports "dynamic" mapping only, applied heuristic.
```

sasha: that WARN is suspicious. rope_scaling linear->dynamic heuristics can subtly change phase in long-range queries. could explain truncation/regression.

lina.k: reproduction steps I've used: 
1) HF tarball -> hf2rw conversion script (master)
2) run unit token-level comparison (unquant)
3) run quantized eval harness (int4)

Observations: unquant diff small when we force preserve num_key_value_heads, but quantized outputs diverge badly when RW remaps heads or reduces max_pos.

matt: possible approaches: 
- prefer preserving num_key_value_heads and adjust heads_per_head dim compute path (risky)
- or keep RW mapping but add a conversion-time warning and per-model eval threshold failing CI

carlos: can we detect sliding_window semantics mismatch? HF uses sliding_window to indicate KV cache window (like 256) while RW expects sliding_window to be a boolean-ish mode flag in some older models. conversion bot might be overwriting.

lina.k: example failing prompt: long system message + 1k token user -> model hallucinated early end-of-sequence. logs show attention weirdness at positions ~900-1100.

sasha: TL;DR: rope_scaling + max_position_embeddings and num_key_value_heads need an explicit mapping check in convert script, and conversion should preserve sliding_window semantics, not clobber.

matt: I can put up a tiny patch that: 
- detects rope_scaling.type != "dynamic" and flags for manual review,
- if num_key_value_heads present, try to compute and keep a "kv_head_remap" table instead of deleting the field,
- preserves max_position_embeddings and emits fallback only if runtime can't allocate.

carlos: please also add a unit test in hf-convert tests: generate a synthetic model config with rope_scaling factor != 1 + num_key_value_heads != heads_per_layer / n and assert convert does NOT silently drop fields.

convert-bot: created PR #3789 (convert/hf: preserve kv heads + rope check) and added failing test case.

lina.k: testing PR now on quant pipeline. will report back with eval diffs.

sasha: also add a note in model-onboarding checklist: "check rope_scaling semantics + sliding_window behaviour in HF configs; run long-context regression harness if max_position_embeddings > 1024"

matt: agreed. if we can't map automatically we should fail the conversion and require manual opt-in with a conversion config.

lina.k: quick interim patch: I ran convert-bot but overrode max_position_embeddings->2048 and forced preserve num_key_value_heads. quant eval improved from 23%->87% on our reference prompts. not final but promising.

carlos: awesome. keep the failing logs and attach to PR. ping me when you have the eval artifacts.

sasha: thanks — would be nice to add a diagnostic output that shows pre/post attention KV shapes and a small per-layer checksum to detect silent remaps in future.

lina.k: will add to the PR. last message for now: folks, watch out for HF forks that encode sliding_window inconsistently — we should whitelist acceptable patterns in conversion docs. :warning:
